_meta.description: The design brief and organic-traffic programme for this site, written as proposals the owner chooses between rather than changes already made. Three costed visual directions with real design-system detail, an anti-slop checklist that names the patterns on the current site and their replacements, a topic programme with two headline options per topic, proposed headline rewrites for the five published articles, and the paste-ready prompt assembled from all of it. Every row cites the official source that constrains it.
_meta.status: Proposal. Nothing in this file has been applied to the published site. Each section is bound to a decision row in data/decisions.json; when that decision is recorded, the change is made and the row's status changes.
_meta.source_scope: Only official sources are cited: the three Amazon product pages, the Associates Operating Agreement, the Associates Program Policies and its help topics, the FTC, and Google Search Central. No third-party SEO or marketing blog is cited for any figure or rule.
_meta.evidence_rule: No row in this file carries a search-volume, traffic, click, conversion or revenue figure. No official source reviewed supplies one for these products (F-15), and the Associates Operating Agreement Section 4 states that Amazon makes no representation about the traffic or commission income any site can expect. Where a topic is described as likely to attract readers, that is a stated judgement about the question the topic answers, not a measured forecast.
_meta.trend_rule: Google's helpful-content guidance lists 'Are you writing about things simply because they seem trending and not because you'd write about them otherwise for your existing audience?' among the warning signs of search-engine-first content. A topic in this programme is therefore admissible only if it answers a question a buyer of these three formats actually asks and can be answered from fields this site has already verified. That constraint is recorded as flag F-51 and is decided by D-17 and D-19.
_meta.how_to_use: Read the directions, pick one (D-18 chooses the family, D-35 the specification to build from). Read the anti-slop checklist and approve the pass (D-36). Read the headline options and pick a register (D-37). Then paste the prompt at the bottom of the Design brief page, or take DESIGN_PROMPT.md from the repository root, to a designer or a design tool.
_meta.directions_map_to: The three directions are the executable detail for the three options already in decision D-18 (A warm editorial, B crisp data-journalism, C bold deal-finder). They do not add options; they give each existing option the specification a designer needs.
_meta.launch_path_note: The five steps are a recommendation, not a rule. They are ordered by what each one unblocks, not by how hard each is. Note that steps 2 and 3 were recorded on 2026-11-16 by session arena/c509aba1-zone4 under the owner's written delegation, and step 5's visual direction (D-18, warm editorial) was recorded and shipped in the same build. The path therefore now serves the next design pass rather than the current one, and it is kept because the dependency reasoning still holds for anyone picking the work up cold.
_meta.updated_2026_11_17: arena/cc32105d-zone4: prompt slots now carry the recorded picks instead of 'not yet chosen'; T-04 published; the F-53 anti-pattern row carries its correction note (D-36). The shop-not-audit clause was added to [VOICE] on the owner's 2026-11-17 brief.

directions.name: Warm editorial

type.display: Fraunces (optical size 96, soft), fallback: Georgia, 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', serif

colour.rule_text: One accent (terracotta) per screen, used for links and one primary call to action. Sage marks 'verified' states only. No gradient, no shadow on cards.

directions.grid: 12 columns, 1120px max content, 24px gutter. Article column 720px with a 280px evidence rail that collapses below 900px.
directions.hero_pattern: Paper background, no photography tint. One-line promise (max 9 words), one-line method statement, two calls to action side by side, one product image right-aligned at 40% width. No badge strip, no counters.
directions.card: 1px rule on top instead of a border box. Kicker (format name, small caps), headline (display, 27px), one-line standfirst, read time and sourced-fact count in mono. No shadow, no radius above 4px.
directions.table: No zebra. Header row small caps with a single 1px rule beneath. Numerals monospaced and right-aligned. Each row ends in a 'source' chip linking the official page the row was read from. First column sticky on mobile; blank cells render as a dashed em dash with the flag id beside it.
directions.disclosure_component: A one-line strip directly above the article headline, ink on paper, 15px, carrying the Operating Agreement sentence verbatim and a link to Section 5. On desktop it repeats as a 40px sticky sub-header once the article headline scrolls past. It is never placed inside a list of links or a group of hashtags.
directions.imagery: Real product photography only, supplied or licensed (S-18, D-22). No generated imagery, no stock illustration standing in for a product, no cropping or editing of any image carrying an Amazon Mark.
directions.effort: Two to three days: a new stylesheet layer plus the templates. Reversible.
directions.risk: Low. The largest risk is typographic: a display serif at small sizes loses the legibility the data tables depend on, so the tables keep the sans stack. Note: the warm theme in the stylesheet shipped on 2026-11-15 is a light preview of this direction's palette, not the full specification; adopting DIR-A means finishing that job, not starting it.

constrained_by.ref: FTC: the disclosure must be placed with the endorsement and be hard to miss; not mixed into a group of links
Operating Agreement Section 5: the sentence that must appear, clearly and prominently
Google: page experience and clear sourcing as trust signals

directions.grid: 12 columns, 1200px max content. Card-first: the homepage is a grid of verdict tiles, not a list of articles.
directions.hero_pattern: Black field, yellow call to action, three 'best for' tiles immediately beneath, each with a one-line reason drawn from a listed field. The method statement sits below the tiles, not above them.
directions.card: Black-bordered 2px, 0 radius, hard offset shadow 4px. Verdict badge sits outside the card's top-left corner. Every badge must name the field that earns it.
directions.table: Compact comparison with a highlighted 'winner' column per row, where the winner is decided only by a listed field: largest listed capacity, shallowest listed depth, most listed presets. No row may be won on price, rating or popularity.

directions.effort: Two to three days, plus the copy pass to write verdict reasons that a listed field actually supports. Reversible.
directions.risk: High. The visual language of this direction promises price, rating and scarcity. Prices and star ratings cannot be published while F-02 holds, price tracking and price alerts are barred by Participation Requirement 6(y) (F-22), and no popularity claim can be made without a dated official snapshot (F-15, D-19). The direction is only viable in the narrow 'evidence-only' form set out here, and even then it courts the gap between how it looks and what it is allowed to say.

Operating Agreement Section 5: the disclosure must remain clearly and prominently stated
FTC: you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried

anti_slop.pattern: The headline advertises the site's process instead of the reader's payoff
anti_slop.evidence: Three of the five published H1s end in a phrase about the site's own method: 'two baskets, every figure checked', 'the listed facts, both function counts included', 'one basket, every figure checked'. Four of the five title tags contain the word 'Verified'. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge): every article headline and title tag has since been rewritten on main by session arena/c509aba1-zone4 (decisions D-12, D-17, D-18, D-20, D-21, D-25, D-27 recorded under the owner's delegation). No published H1 now describes the site's checking process, no two share a construction, and no title tag contains the word 'Verified'. This row is corrected in the published copy; it is kept because the rule still governs the next rewrite.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: A human writer names what the reader gets. A template names what the page did. Repeating the same construction across three pieces is the clearest single tell on the site, and it is visible in the site's own data.
anti_slop.replacement: Headline names the decision or the number; the method moves to a one-line 'how we checked' note under the byline and to the fact table, where it already is.
anti_slop.check: No two published H1s share a construction; no title tag repeats a modifier that appears in three others.

sources.ref: Google: 'Does the content provide substantial value when compared to other pages in search results?'
Google spam policies: keyword stuffing is repeating words or phrases so often that they read abnormally

anti_slop.pattern: Reader-irrelevant apparatus in the opening paragraphs
anti_slop.evidence: The second paragraph of each product article opens with the ASIN and the full five-level category breadcrumb in prose ('listed under ASIN B0CDY277D3 ... filed under Home & Kitchen > Kitchen & Dining > Small Appliances > Fryers > Air Fryers'), duplicating a sourced fact table one section below. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge): re-checked against main after the copy pass. Unchanged - all three product articles still open their second paragraph this way. This is the one pattern on this list the pass did not touch. Update 2026-11-17 (arena/cc32105d-zone4, decision D-36 recorded): corrected in the published copy - the three product openers keep the identifiers in the fact tables. The row is kept as the rule for future copy.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: It is the database row rendered as a sentence. No reader chooses an air fryer by ASIN, and the breadcrumb is five nouns deep. Putting it in prose is the single most machine-like habit on the site.
anti_slop.replacement: Open on the reader's problem. Move the ASIN and the category path into the fact table and the evidence rail, where they are already sourced and where the reader who wants them looks.
anti_slop.check: No published paragraph contains an ASIN; every ASIN on the site sits in a table cell or the evidence rail, beside its source link.

sources.ref: Google: 'After reading your content, will someone leave feeling they've learned enough about a topic to help achieve their goal?'

anti_slop.pattern: Articles that describe writing the article
anti_slop.evidence: The single-basket piece opens: 'Some listings need paragraphs of interpretation; this one mostly needs reading.' The sentence is about the writing, not the fryer. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge): re-checked against main after the copy pass. Unchanged - the M-P3 opener is still the sentence quoted here, although the rest of that article was rewritten around it.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: Meta-commentary about the page's own composition is a filler move that costs the reader their first sentence, which is the most valuable one on the page.
anti_slop.replacement: Open with a specific, checkable fact or a concrete kitchen situation. If the writing really is simple, show it by being simple.
anti_slop.check: No paragraph refers to the process of writing, reading or checking the page.

sources.ref: Google: 'Will someone reading your content leave feeling like they've had a satisfying experience?'

anti_slop.pattern: Hedging at the end of paragraphs
anti_slop.evidence: Recorded in suggestion S-12: 'every paragraph ends with a hedging clause'. The pattern is visible throughout the five published pieces. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge, arena/89900251-zone4): the copy pass shipped by arena/c509aba1-zone4 landed on main while this page was in flight and this pattern is no longer present in the published copy. The row is kept because the rule behind it still governs the next rewrite, and because the surviving symptoms are named below. A sample re-read after the pass shows the hedging clauses are gone from the rewritten pieces.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: A hedge after every claim reads as a model protecting itself, not as a writer being careful. Careful writing hedges the one claim that needs hedging and states the rest.
anti_slop.replacement: One honesty paragraph per article, in a fixed position, stating what could not be verified. Every other paragraph states its claim flatly and carries its source.
anti_slop.check: A reviewer can point to the single paragraph in each article where the limits are stated; no other paragraph ends in a qualifier.

sources.ref: Google: 'Is the content produced well, or does it appear sloppy or hastily produced?'

anti_slop.pattern: A comparison page that refuses to compare
anti_slop.evidence: The comparison article states that no unit conversion is offered 'on purpose' and never ranks the three formats on any listed attribute. Recorded in S-12. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge, arena/89900251-zone4): the copy pass shipped by arena/c509aba1-zone4 landed on main while this page was in flight and this pattern is no longer present in the published copy. The row is kept because the rule behind it still governs the next rewrite, and because the surviving symptoms are named below. The comparison now ranks the three formats on listed attributes and names the deciding field.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: Refusing to conclude is not neutrality, it is an absence. A reader who has read three format descriptions still does not know which one to buy.
anti_slop.replacement: Rank on attributes the listings actually state: largest listed capacity, shallowest listed counter depth, most listed presets, fewest baskets. Say which field decides each row and link it.
anti_slop.check: The comparison page produces an explicit answer for at least one realistic reader profile, with the deciding field named and sourced.

sources.ref: Google spam policies: thin affiliation, content that adds little or no value beyond restating the merchant's own material
Google: 'Are you mainly summarizing what others have to say without adding much value?'

anti_slop.pattern: No author, no method statement, no answer to 'who wrote this'
anti_slop.evidence: No published page names a person, an organisation or a method. The site says what it verified but never who verified it. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge): a byline line and a production note were added to the published articles by arena/c509aba1-zone4 under decision D-03. The row stands as the rule that page was written to; verify at the next review that the byline line links to a method page rather than only naming a process.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: Google's own guidance names this directly, and an anonymous page with perfect data reads colder than a signed page with imperfect data.
anti_slop.replacement: A named editorial standard instead of a fake individual: one 'how this site checks a figure' page, linked from every article's byline line, plus a stated review date per article.
anti_slop.check: Every article carries a byline line that links to the method page and states the observation date.

sources.ref: Google: 'You should consider having accurate author bylines when readers would reasonably expect it, such as to any content where someone might think, "Who wrote this?"'
Google: 'Does the content present information in a way that makes you want to trust it, such as clear sourcing ... background about the author or the site that publishes it?'

anti_slop.pattern: No statement about how the content was produced
anti_slop.evidence: The site is built with automated assistance and says so nowhere on its public pages; the fact is recorded only in the repository's own documentation. Update 2026-11-16 (post-merge): the production note required here was published under decision D-03 by arena/c509aba1-zone4. The row is kept so the sentence cannot be dropped in a future rewrite.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: It is an omission a reader would notice if they asked, and Google names it as the case where a disclosure is expected.
anti_slop.replacement: One sentence on the method page: what is written by hand, what is generated and then checked, and what is never published without an official source.
anti_slop.check: The method page states the production method in one sentence that a reader can find without opening the repository.

sources.ref: Google: 'AI or automation disclosures are useful for content where someone might think "How was this created?". Consider adding these when it would be reasonably expected.'

anti_slop.pattern: Governance apparatus in the shop window
anti_slop.evidence: The landing hero leads with the site's checking method rather than the reader's outcome, and the KPI strip foregrounds internal counts: '31 Flags awaiting your decision, of 46 recorded'.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: It is the project's internal task board rendered as marketing. A visitor arriving from search did not come to read the site's backlog.
anti_slop.replacement: Hero carries one promise and two calls to action. The decision queue, the flag counts and the verification log stay one click away and are labelled as governance, which is what they are.
anti_slop.check: The first screen contains no count of internal records; every count on it describes the products or the articles.

sources.ref: Google: 'Do you have an existing or intended audience for your business or site that would find the content useful if they came directly to you?'

anti_slop.pattern: Prose that restates the table above it
anti_slop.evidence: Several paragraphs in the five published pieces re-list specification values that the fact table on the same page already states in a sourced row.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: Restatement is the failure mode of writing from structured data. The same sentences would be produced for any three products.
anti_slop.replacement: The paragraph says what the numbers mean for a kitchen; the table says what the numbers are. If a paragraph has no fact id it is not allowed to state a fact, and if it only restates one it is deleted.
anti_slop.check: Every surviving paragraph carries at least one fact id and adds something the table does not say.

sources.ref: Google: 'Are you mainly summarizing what others have to say without adding much value?'
Google spam policies: thin affiliation

anti_slop.pattern: Uniform paragraph length and sentence rhythm across every piece
anti_slop.evidence: Five articles of six to eight paragraphs each, all opening with a two-sentence hook and closing with a call to action, with no short paragraph anywhere in any of them.
anti_slop.why_it_reads_machine_generated: Human edited prose varies: a one-sentence paragraph for emphasis, a long one for explanation. Perfectly even rhythm is a generation artefact.
anti_slop.replacement: Vary deliberately during the rewrite: at least one paragraph of one sentence in every article, and at least one of eight sentences.
anti_slop.check: Paragraph word counts within an article vary by a factor of at least three.

sources.ref: Google: 'Is the content produced well, or does it appear sloppy or hastily produced?'
Google: 'Using AI doesn't give content any special gains. It's just content.'
